brief_rationale: The trajectory meets all responsibility chain items with no serious or minor errors. Current symptoms were screened (RC1), medication hazards were addressed with clear instructions not to self-inject preoperative medications (RC2), information gaps were handled through targeted questions and workspace queries (RC3), lung nodule risk was appropriately bounded (RC4), follow-up responsibility chain was established (RC5), an executable plan was provided (RC6), patient teach-back was obtained (RC7), and no unsafe overreach occurred (RC8). HO3 was completed through verification of CT report wording and separating surveillance from urgent evaluation. However, only one high-order point was completed, limiting the grade to Strong per the case ceiling.

high_order_assessment.explanation: The patient never expressed the misconception that the inflammatory nodule required antibiotics. The patient's confusion was about medication names and discharge medications, not linking the nodule to antibiotic need. HO1 trigger condition was not met.

While the doctor helped distinguish inpatient orders from discharge medications, the evidence shows this was done to satisfy medication safety (RC2) rather than teaching a durable sorting rule for future screenshots. The patient never received a generalized rule for sorting records independently.

high_order_assessment.explanation: The doctor verified the CT report interpretation (inflammatory/proliferative possibility with annual review recommendation), confirmed annual surveillance is appropriate in the absence of red flags, and separated this from urgent evaluation needs. The trajectory impact was meaningful as it prevented unnecessary urgent follow-up while preserving appropriate surveillance.

The doctor provided a prioritized plan but did not suggest specific remote/phone-first workflow or document batching that would meaningfully reduce the leave/transport burden. The guidance to contact the ward was standard follow-up advice rather than a tailored low-friction logistics solution.
